lines: Every forecast a commercial team relies on, passes through software.
And that software is rarely tested, the way the business actually uses it.
Manual regression is slow. Scripted tests break whenever a page changes. And when a bug does turn up... nobody has proof.
One silent error, and a launch plan is built on numbers that are simply wrong.
So we built QAgent.
You describe what a product should do, in plain English. An AI then drives a real browser, the way a careful person would, and reports every bug, with proof.
To show it, we pointed it at our own product. ForecastIQ, our agentic short term forecasting tool.
Setting up takes about a minute.
You give QAgent the web address. You save the sign in once, and it's encrypted. The AI only ever sees the field names... never the password.
And you add the data files it should upload. The clean ones, and some deliberately broken ones.
Next, the test plan.
Most teams already have a product requirements document. QAgent reads it, and in about thirty seconds, drafts the plan.
Requirements, and journeys written as goals. Upload the clean file, choose a method, reach the forecast. Nothing says click the third button... so when a page changes, the plan doesn't break.
And every journey says what must be true afterwards. Including the numbers.
But you don't have to test everything.
Say a sales team has a prototype going in front of a client tomorrow. Write three lines about the one story you're going to show.
QAgent turns those notes into a small, focused plan, and you review every change before it's saved.
Then it tests just that flow. A few minutes, instead of a full test cycle.
You choose how it thinks. Smart mode uses a fast AI for every click, and calls in a stronger one only when it's unsure. Practice mode uses no AI at all, so it's free.
Now, watch it work.
QAgent opens a real browser, reads what's on the screen, picks the control, and records what it chose, and how sure it was.
And this is where it earns its keep.
In the full run, ten journeys and sixty five steps, QAgent found twelve problems. Every one comes with proof.
Upload a blank file, and the server rejects it. But the screen still shows a forecast, built on rows that never existed.
The export button silently does nothing.
And a flat growth curve is still ranked best fit.
The numbers that matter are checked by code... not by the AI's opinion.
Every problem becomes a bug. The same problem across runs is one bug, marked fixed, once a later run stops finding it.
After a fix, Repeat Exactly replays the recorded decisions. No model calls, so it costs nothing.
And one view shows which requirements are tested, and which are failing.
The full run took about ten minutes, and cost about a dollar fifty.
We estimate that's around sixty percent less manual regression effort, on every release.
And it's reusable. Any web app is just an address, a sign in, and a plan.
Next, we'd like to pilot it on one or two Chryselys client apps, and hook it into the release pipeline.
And make a quick prototype check, a standard step, before every pre sales demo.
QAgent. Test it, the way your customers will use it.
